design.voice_description: A real man in his early thirties with a natural American accent, talking to a friend about a small tool he built and genuinely likes. Relaxed, warm and a little understated, low mid-range voice with some natural breath and texture. Conversational rhythm, unhurried, with tiny natural pauses. Not a radio announcer, not a commercial voice, no forced enthusiasm, no vocal fry. Close microphone, dry quiet room, clean studio-quality recording.

music_prompt: Calm minimal electronic background for a software product demo. Soft warm synth pads, gentle plucked arpeggio, light airy percussion, steady 100 BPM, modern and clean, no vocals, no big drops, even energy throughout, ends softly.
text:
Meet Snap. A free, open-source screenshot tool for Windows.

Press Scroll Lock, and the screen freezes. Move your cursor, and Snap finds every element underneath it. Scroll to grab a bigger area, or a smaller one.

Hold Control, and mark it up right there. Boxes, arrows, numbered steps. Hit Enter, and it's on your clipboard.

Need more? Open the editor. Blur anything private, add a note, and every change is copied automatically.

It records video too, up to a hundred and twenty frames per second. Saved as an MP4, and one click turns it into a GIF.

Snap. Free, on GitHub.
